title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Premium Revision Paper #20

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #20
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these gives the young plant its first food before its leaves open? (1 mark)
   A. The wind
   B. The flower
   C. The bark
   D. The seed

2. Which of these is a way that people benefit from plants? (1 mark)
   A. They give plastic
   B. They cause floods
   C. They give food, shade and wood
   D. They make noise

3. Why should you not pull leaves off a young plant for fun? (1 mark)
   A. Leaves are heavy
   B. The leaves make the roots sweet
   C. The plant has too many leaves
   D. The plant needs its leaves to make food

4. A student puts a plant in a box with a small hole on one side. After a week, the plant bends toward the hole. This shows that plants (1 mark)
   A. need no water
   B. respond to light
   C. walk
   D. make sound

5. Why do farmers remove weeds from a crop field? (1 mark)
   A. To harm the crops
   B. To make weeds grow
   C. So crops get enough water, light and space
   D. To stop rain falling

6. Which of these animals lays eggs? (1 mark)
   A. Hen
   B. Cow
   C. Human
   D. Goat

7. Which of these parts is found after the stomach? (1 mark)
   A. Mouth
   B. Gullet
   C. Tongue
   D. Small intestine

8. What is absorption? (1 mark)
   A. Chewing food
   B. Swallowing food
   C. Passing faeces
   D. Digested food passing into the blood

9. Which of these is a symptom of an unhealthy digestive system? (1 mark)
   A. Sunburn
   B. Sneezing
   C. Stomach ache
   D. A headache only

10. Why is it important to eat slowly? (1 mark)
   A. It makes you thirsty
   B. It lets you chew well and helps digestion
   C. It stops you growing
   D. It makes food taste of salt

11. Why should fruits and vegetables be washed before eating? (1 mark)
   A. To remove dirt and germs
   B. To make them sweeter
   C. To make them heavier
   D. To make them hot

12. In the dry tissue experiment, why does the tissue stay dry? (1 mark)
   A. The tissue is warm
   B. Air in the cup keeps the water out
   C. Water cannot touch paper
   D. The cup is made of plastic

13. Which of these is true of a solid? (1 mark)
   A. It has no mass
   B. It keeps its shape wherever it is put
   C. It cannot be measured
   D. It takes the shape of any container

14. Which state of matter has its own shape and fixed volume? (1 mark)
   A. Steam only
   B. Gas
   C. Liquid
   D. Solid

15. Which grouping of gases is correct? (1 mark)
   A. Air, steam and cooking gas are gases
   B. Stone, water and wood are liquids
   C. Sugar, oil and air are solids
   D. Milk, chalk and steam are solids

16. A heavy sack of maize has more mass than a small packet of salt. This means the sack has more (1 mark)
   A. Light
   B. Sound
   C. Matter
   D. Air only

17. What does a football need to keep its shape? (1 mark)
   A. Air
   B. Sand
   C. Milk
   D. Water

18. What is the danger of leaving plastic bags on the ground? (1 mark)
   A. They make the soil rich
   B. They stay for a long time and block drains
   C. They turn into soil fast
   D. They grow into plants

19. Why is broken glass on the ground dangerous? (1 mark)
   A. It rots
   B. It grows
   C. It feeds the soil
   D. It can cut people and animals

20. Which of these is NOT a way of managing solid waste? (1 mark)
   A. Throwing it in a river
   B. Reusing
   C. Recycling
   D. Composting

21. A wrapper of biscuits is made of plastic. Which type of waste is it? (1 mark)
   A. Non-decomposable
   B. Gas
   C. Decomposable
   D. Liquid

22. What is decomposable waste? (1 mark)
   A. Waste that rots and breaks down
   B. Waste that never changes
   C. Waste made of metal
   D. Waste made of plastic

23. Which waste can be reused as a pencil holder? (1 mark)
   A. Banana peel
   B. An empty tin
   C. Old leaves
   D. Egg shells

24. What is a good use of old clothes? (1 mark)
   A. Throw them in a drain
   B. Use them as cleaning cloths
   C. Burn them near a house
   D. Bury them in a garden pit

25. What should you wear when collecting waste? (1 mark)
   A. Sandals only
   B. Nothing
   C. A hat only
   D. Gloves and closed shoes

26. How does mulching help save water? (1 mark)
   A. It reduces evaporation from the soil
   B. It makes soil hot
   C. It makes soil dry
   D. It makes water flow away

27. Which of these can make a river dry up? (1 mark)
   A. Planting trees
   B. Cutting trees near it and wasting water
   C. Saving water
   D. Using rain tanks

28. A jerrycan holds 20 litres. A leaking tap wastes 40 litres in a day. How many jerrycans is that? (1 mark)
   A. 60
   B. 2
   C. 4
   D. 20

29. What is the job of the gutter in rainwater harvesting? (1 mark)
   A. Stores water
   B. Heats water
   C. Cleans water
   D. Carries water from the roof to a pipe

30. Which of these is an example of reducing water wastage? (1 mark)
   A. Closing a tap after use
   B. Washing with lots of water
   C. Ignoring leaks
   D. Leaving the hose on

31. Which of these is a pull? (1 mark)
   A. Kicking a ball
   B. Opening a drawer by its handle
   C. Closing a door by pushing
   D. Pressing a bell

32. What should you do when doing force experiments? (1 mark)
   A. Keep fingers away from moving parts
   B. Push others
   C. Throw heavy things
   D. Run with sharp tools

33. A rolling ball slowly comes to a stop on the ground mainly because of (1 mark)
   A. Light
   B. Colour
   C. Sound
   D. Friction

34. A ball is rolling and you kick it in the direction it moves. What happens? (1 mark)
   A. It changes into a solid
   B. It speeds up
   C. It gets smaller
   D. It stops

35. What is the purpose of skylights? (1 mark)
   A. Let daylight through the roof
   B. Make the house hot
   C. Block light
   D. Let rain in on purpose

36. Which of these is a torch used for? (1 mark)
   A. To make food
   B. To cool a room
   C. To give light in the dark
   D. To make sound

37. Which small living thing makes its own light and so is a natural source? (1 mark)
   A. Firefly
   B. Torch
   C. Electric bulb
   D. Candle

38. Which use of heat helps us on a cold morning? (1 mark)
   A. Keeping us warm
   B. Growing shadows
   C. Making things dark
   D. Making sound

39. Why do we boil water before drinking if it may be unsafe? (1 mark)
   A. Heat removes all salt
   B. Heat makes water heavy
   C. Heat kills germs
   D. Heat makes water sweet

40. Where should children be when an adult is cooking? (1 mark)
   A. On top of the cooker
   B. Away from the fire
   C. Holding the pot
   D. Next to the fire

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Write the function of the rectum and anus. (3 marks)

42. List four water-saving habits that pupils can practise at school. (4 marks)

43. Explain how gravity helps and how it can cause problems in daily life. (5 marks)

44. Convert 4 kg into grams. (2 marks)

45. Describe what you would put in a portfolio about vertebrates and invertebrates. (4 marks)

46. Explain why a mirror or a shiny cup is not a source of light. (3 marks)

47. Describe how rainwater can be harvested from a school roof. (3 marks)

48. Define matter and give two examples. (2 marks)

49. Give three safety measures to observe when cooking. (3 marks)

50. Draw and label a plant showing roots, stem, leaves and flower. (4 marks)

51. Give three ways of lighting a house at night. (3 marks)

52. Describe how you would measure 300 ml of water using a measuring jug, and how you would measure the mass of a mango. (5 marks)

53. Name two roots, two stems and two leaves that people eat. (4 marks)

54. A bat has wings. Explain why it is not a bird. (3 marks)

55. Why is chewing food well important? (2 marks)

56. State two functions of roots. (2 marks)

57. Explain why we should wash our hands before eating and after using the toilet. (3 marks)

58. Explain why plastic bags are a danger to the environment. (3 marks)

59. What is the difference between a vertebrate and an invertebrate? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #20 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — The seed
   The seed contains stored food that feeds the young plant at first.

2. C — They give food, shade and wood
   Plants give us food, shade, medicine, wood and clean air.

3. D — The plant needs its leaves to make food
   Leaves are the food factories of the plant.

4. B — respond to light
   The plant responds to the light entering through the hole.

5. C — So crops get enough water, light and space
   Weeds compete with crops for water, light and room.

6. A — Hen
   A hen lays eggs. The others give birth to live young.

7. D — Small intestine
   Food moves from the stomach to the small intestine.

8. D — Digested food passing into the blood
   Absorption means digested food parts pass into the blood.

9. C — Stomach ache
   Stomach ache, bloating, diarrhoea, vomiting and constipation are digestive symptoms.

10. B — It lets you chew well and helps digestion
   Chewing well breaks food down before swallowing.

11. A — To remove dirt and germs
   Washing removes dirt, germs and worm eggs.

12. B — Air in the cup keeps the water out
   Air takes up the space inside the cup.

13. B — It keeps its shape wherever it is put
   A solid has a definite shape.

14. D — Solid
   Solids keep their shape and volume.

15. A — Air, steam and cooking gas are gases
   Air, steam and cooking gas are gases.

16. C — Matter
   Mass is the amount of matter.

17. A — Air
   The air inside fills the football.

18. B — They stay for a long time and block drains
   Plastic bags stay for years and block drains.

19. D — It can cut people and animals
   Sharp glass can injure.

20. A — Throwing it in a river
   Throwing waste in rivers pollutes water.

21. A — Non-decomposable
   Plastic wrappers do not rot easily.

22. A — Waste that rots and breaks down
   Decomposable waste is broken down by decomposers.

23. B — An empty tin
   A clean tin can be reused.

24. B — Use them as cleaning cloths
   Reusing old cloth as cleaning cloths reduces waste.

25. D — Gloves and closed shoes
   Gloves and shoes protect from cuts and germs.

26. A — It reduces evaporation from the soil
   Covered soil stays moist longer.

27. B — Cutting trees near it and wasting water
   Cutting trees near sources reduces water.

28. B — 2
   40 divided by 20 = 2.

29. D — Carries water from the roof to a pipe
   Gutters catch water as it runs off the roof.

30. A — Closing a tap after use
   Closing taps stops the flow of water.

31. B — Opening a drawer by its handle
   A handle is pulled toward you.

32. A — Keep fingers away from moving parts
   Safe practice prevents injuries.

33. D — Friction
   Friction between the ball and the ground slows it.

34. B — It speeds up
   A force in the direction of movement increases speed.

35. A — Let daylight through the roof
   Skylights are roof openings or sheets that let light in.

36. C — To give light in the dark
   A torch is an artificial light source.

37. A — Firefly
   Fireflies make their own light.

38. A — Keeping us warm
   Heat keeps our bodies warm.

39. C — Heat kills germs
   Boiling kills many germs.

40. B — Away from the fire
   Children stay away from the cooker.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: The rectum stores faeces for a short time and the anus is the opening through which faeces leave the body.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rectum, 1 mark for anus, 1 mark for describing waste leaving.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Close taps, report leaks, use a bucket for watering the garden, water plants in the morning or evening, use a cup to drink.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: It keeps us on the ground, makes rain fall and water flow downhill. It can make objects fall and cause injuries and break things.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for help and 2 marks for problems and 1 mark for a clear explanation.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: 4000 g.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 4 x 1000 and 1 mark for the answer with units.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: A drawing of each animal, its name, whether it is a vertebrate or invertebrate, one sign of life seen, put together in a folder.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four items.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: It does not make its own light. It only reflects light that falls on it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for not making light, 1 mark for reflecting, 1 mark for explanation.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Rain falls on the roof and runs into the gutter. The gutter leads to a pipe which fills a covered tank.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for roof and gutter, 1 mark for pipe, 1 mark for tank.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: Matter is anything that has mass and takes up space. Examples: water, stone, air.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for two examples.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use gloves, turn handles inwards, keep children away, do not play with matches, keep paraffin away from fire.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: A drawing with four correctly labelled parts: roots below the ground, stem upright, leaves on the stem and a flower at the top.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correctly drawn and labelled part.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Electric bulbs, solar lamps, paraffin lamps, candles.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

52. (5 marks)
   Answer: Place the jug on a flat surface, pour water until the level reaches the 300 mark with your eye level with the water. For the mango, place it on a balance and read the mass in grams.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for flat surface, pouring to 300 ml, eye level, using a balance, reading in grams.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: Roots: carrot, cassava, sweet potato. Stems: sugarcane. Leaves: cabbage, sukuma wiki, spinach (any two of each, with correct grouping).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair and 1 mark for correct grouping overall.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: A bat has fur and feeds its young on milk. Birds have feathers and lay eggs. So a bat is a mammal.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for fur, 1 mark for milk, 1 mark for mammal.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: It breaks food into small pieces and makes digestion easier.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for small pieces and 1 mark for easier digestion.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: They hold the plant in the soil and take in water and mineral salts. Some store food.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct function.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: Hands may carry germs and worm eggs. Washing removes them and stops them entering the mouth and causing disease.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for germs on hands, 1 mark for washing removes them, 1 mark for preventing illness.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: They stay for many years, block drains, harm animals that eat them and pollute land and water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of three points.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: A vertebrate has a backbone and an invertebrate has no backbone.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.
